mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within the last month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within the last month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increases and negative 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth over two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations adjust downward.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between GDPC1 declines and negative 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% in the last month signals a strengthening supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as increased production capacity supports economic growth and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment, indicated by CPIAUCSL remaining below 2% for three consecutive months, signals a stable monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors favor equities in a low-inflation, low-interest-rate environment.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 60-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between low CPIAUCSL and positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in housing starts (HOUST) and a decrease in retail sales (RSAFS) over the last month indicates a shift in consumer spending from goods to housing, which historically correlates with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the housing sector gains momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases and RSAFS decreases in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint behavior of HOUST and RSAFS does not significantly predict positive 20-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in the last month, coupled with an increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.3%, signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decrease > 100k and UNRATE increase > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the joint behavior of PAYEMS and UNRATE does not significantly predict negative 5-day returns (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on signal where the S&P 500 tends to produce positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days when the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below the historical average, as lower rates typically support equity valuations.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative 20-day returns in more than 50% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is below its historical average, or if the correlation between low FEDFUNDS and positive 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
